_doc: 1.0. The twenty faction missions, from missions.md and lore.md: four chains of five, one to a faction, each with a fixed advisor who is met in the world. Nothing is accepted from a board: the advisor offers the next mission in person, the work is done at 'site' (a landmark id, or 'district:NAME' for an ordinary building in that district - the thing is in one of the containers there, and a thorough search cannot miss it), and it is reported back to the advisor in person, where the decision is made. A chain is strictly in order; the chains do not depend on each other. 'xpShare' is the share of the story award each resolution pays. Each choice: cash, standing by faction, and a flag that is kept on the profile for good (later missions and the world read it).

advisors.name: Nika Beridze
advisors.greeting: Beridze. I assess claims for Halberd. Somebody has to decide what a thing is worth once nobody is left to say it was theirs.
advisors.done: The tracing archive is open to you. It keeps a line on everyone who signed anything in this district - the living and the others. Use it for your own search.

advisors.name: Lt. Vera Sokolova
advisors.greeting: Lieutenant Sokolova. I reconcile passage requests. I have seen what a crowd does when nobody tells it the truth, and what it does when somebody does.
advisors.done: There is an evacuation contact on the verified list who remembers the night you are asking about. I have written you in. That is as far as my signature goes.

advisors.name: Kateryna Melnyk
advisors.greeting: Kateryna. I know how everyone here takes their tea, and who will not eat unless somebody sits with them. Sit down a minute. Then I have something to ask.
advisors.done: Someone who left with our blessing has agreed to carry your question further than I can. I left the light on for them. I will leave it on for you.

advisors.name: Wade Ellis
advisors.greeting: Ellis. I get people from one side of a fence to the other. I am reliable about the getting. Ask me who pays for it another day.
advisors.done: One of the people on that road still writes to somebody you would want to talk to. Take the address. Nobody owns the road - and nobody owns that either.

missions.title: Property of the Absent
missions.find: a sealed package, and its custody receipt
missions.brief: A package was put into safekeeping in a Downtown apartment during the evacuation. It has since been sold as abandoned property, and the buyer wants it. Bring it out through the occupied streets and you get access to our tracing records.
missions.discovery: Household valuables - a wedding service, a child's medal, a watch. A meal is still laid on the table beside the packing boxes. The custody receipt says 'held until our return', and it is signed by the grocer at Meridian Fresh Market.
missions.ask: The buyer's claim is good on paper. The owner's name is on the receipt, and one of that family is still alive in the district.

choices.label: Honour the buyer's claim
choices.outcome: Halberd is paid and remembers who delivered. The table in that apartment stays laid for nobody.

choices.label: Return it to the surviving owner
choices.outcome: The owner will not forget it, and neither will the neighbours. The contract is now in dispute, and Nika has to write that down.

missions.lead: The receipt was countersigned at the grocery. Somebody there was taking valuables in for more than safekeeping.

missions.title: Paid in Advance
missions.find: the neighbourhood's old delivery ledger
missions.brief: That receipt leads to Meridian Fresh Market. A carrier's load of supplies there keeps a protection contract alive if it reaches police headquarters. Find the stock and the paperwork that goes with it.
missions.discovery: The residents pooled what they had - rings, tools, a radio - to pay for deliveries. The old ledger shows a street feeding itself, house by house, before anyone thought to call it charity and send a bill.
missions.ask: The stock is contracted to Halberd. It was paid for by the households in that ledger.

choices.label: Deliver the contracted stock
choices.outcome: The contract holds. Halberd's quartermaster opens the better shelf to you. The street goes on paying for what it already bought.

choices.label: Divert it to the households that paid
choices.outcome: The households eat this month, and they will trade with you at their own doors. Halberd books a contract penalty against your name.

missions.lead: The delivery accounts list escorts who were never paid. One of them has not reported in.

missions.title: Outstanding Wages
missions.find: the escort's pay records, and a casualty report
missions.brief: One of our escorts is missing in a Downtown apartment block. Bring them back before the employer declares desertion - or find out why they will not come.
missions.discovery: The escort stayed to guard the residents after the wages stopped. The casualty report blames them for losses that happened before they were even deployed. Nika's initials are on it. She signed without checking.
missions.ask: The escort can be returned to service, or released on the evidence of their own pay records.

choices.label: Return the escort to service
choices.outcome: Halberd has its escort back and owes you a favour. The stairwell they were guarding is unguarded tonight.

choices.label: Present the pay records and get them released
choices.outcome: The escort walks free with what they were owed on paper. The residents trust you. Halberd will not lend you a rifle again in a hurry.

missions.lead: The disputed report names a recovery job in the Industrial district - a data drive in the plant offices.

missions.title: The Cost of Silence
missions.find: the claims drive from the plant offices
missions.brief: There is a data drive in the offices at the Power Plant. Another recovery team is after it. Get there first.
missions.discovery: It is not the cause of anything. It is the claims that were denied afterwards - workers' families, one after another, refused. On the desk a disconnected telephone rings once while you read a message that promises somebody would come back.
missions.ask: The client will pay well for the original and for silence. The claimants could prove their cases with copies.

choices.label: Hand the original to the client
choices.outcome: A substantial payment, and a door at Halberd that used to be closed. The families go on being told there is no record.

choices.label: Give verified copies to the claimants
choices.outcome: The denials can be proved now, and restitution is being demanded in the open. The client has withdrawn its backing from anything with your name on it.

missions.lead: The dispute has come back to where it started: the protection contract, and the people at the grocery who signed it.

missions.title: No Further Obligation
missions.find: the terms of the settlement
missions.brief: The protection contract is being settled at the grocery. See the residents to the table, verify the goods, and keep the exchange from turning into something else.
missions.discovery: The buyer will keep the supplies coming only if the residents sign away their salvage rights. Nika says it out loud, to nobody: a contract can keep a neighbourhood alive and take it away a street at a time.
missions.ask: This becomes how Downtown trades from now on.

choices.label: Enforce exclusivity
choices.outcome: Halberd supplies Downtown reliably and patrols it in strength. What is found there now belongs to the contract.

choices.label: Back the residents' refusal
choices.outcome: Downtown trades for itself, door to door, with thinner protection and nobody's signature on its salvage.

choices.label: Use the plant evidence to force a narrower settlement
choices.outcome: A smaller contract, honestly worded. Neither side got what it wanted, and both signed.

missions.title: Remain Where You Are
missions.find: the evacuation loop, and the patrol's field report
missions.brief: There is a distress call near the airport and a patrol that went to look has not come back. Verify the call. Find the patrol.
missions.discovery: It is the old evacuation recording, still telling people to wait where they are. There are fresh footprints in the dust in front of the speaker. People are still obeying it. The patrol's report and a handful of passage slips are on the desk beside it.
missions.ask: The broadcast can be shut off, or corrected and kept as a beacon.

choices.label: Disable the broadcast
choices.outcome: Nobody else walks to the airport because a dead voice told them to. A landmark that could be heard across the district has gone quiet.

choices.label: Correct it and keep the beacon
choices.outcome: The loop now says where the shelter is. More people will come to an exposed place to hear it.

missions.lead: The passage slips are recent. Somebody at administration is still issuing them.

missions.title: Names at the Gate
missions.find: the applicants' permits, and the gate register
missions.brief: Permit applicants are waiting in the administration buildings. Check their slips against the ones from the airport and see them to the base.
missions.discovery: One household's permit is valid - and leaves out its dependent. The soldiers' register beside it records the night unidentified arrivals killed three people inside the wire. The rule has a reason.
missions.ask: The permit can be enforced as written, or you can vouch for the one it leaves out.

choices.label: Enforce the permit
choices.outcome: The household is separated at the gate. The battalion marks you as someone who follows the paper.

choices.label: Vouch for the dependent
choices.outcome: The household goes through together, on your name. Every search at that gate is slower now, and their passage is your responsibility.

missions.lead: A guard at the gate asks, quietly, about his relief. It is overdue. It went toward the airport.

missions.title: Orders After Dark
missions.find: the relief patrol's kit, laid out and labelled
missions.brief: The relief patrol left its position near the airport. Find it and find out why.
missions.discovery: They are collecting the belongings of the first evacuation - their old comrades', who died waiting for relief that never came. They are finishing somebody else's duty. On the empty channel a voice counts the patrol off, and counts one more than is standing there.
missions.ask: They can be brought back for review, or covered for while they finish.

choices.label: Escort them back for disciplinary review
choices.outcome: The position is manned again and the report is in order. The patrol does not look at you.

choices.label: Cover their absence
choices.outcome: They finish what they went to do, and they will remember who let them. One approach is thinly watched until they are back.

missions.lead: The patrol speaks of two evacuation orders that did not agree. The originals are at administration.

missions.title: The Order That Arrived Late
missions.find: the evacuation orders, with their dispatch stamps
missions.brief: Compare the evacuation orders held at administration with the dispatch times logged at the airport. The route between them is patrolled.
missions.discovery: A real warning reached an official who held it for an hour to avoid a panic. The responders who acted on it were blamed for acting late. It is one preventable loss, inside a disaster nobody could have prevented.
missions.ask: The proof can go up through command, or out to the people it concerns.

choices.label: Submit it through command
choices.outcome: The record is corrected, quietly. Your access stands. The families are not told why.

choices.label: Circulate authenticated copies to survivors
choices.outcome: The survivors know who was blamed for what. The hardliners at the checkpoints have tightened every search because of it.

missions.lead: The precedent is about to be tested. Displaced civilians are asking for a way through to the base, today.

missions.title: The Line We Hold
missions.find: the checkpoint's strength return
missions.brief: Secure one route between administration and the base so the displaced can reach shelter inside the cordon. Walk it first and see what it costs.
missions.discovery: Closing the route protects a checkpoint that has four people left on it, and strands families in buildings with no doors. Opening it means the battalion gives up watching another approach.
missions.ask: This becomes the passage policy for Munincipal.

choices.label: Back strict passage checks
choices.outcome: The cordon holds and fewer are admitted. The checkpoints are thorough, and slow, and sure.

choices.label: Support supervised humanitarian passage
choices.outcome: Civilians move through Munincipal under escort. The perimeter is thinner for it, and everyone on it knows.

missions.title: A Place at the Table
missions.find: a table laid for two, and a care note
missions.brief: A household in Residential has stopped collecting its food. Take them their ration and see how they are. Then I will help you with what you are asking about.
missions.discovery: One resident. Two places set. A recipe in two handwritings and crockery mended so many times it is mostly glue: a long marriage, in a kitchen. Then you look at the second chair again.
missions.ask: They want to stay where they are. The shelter could take them in.

choices.label: Support their choice to remain
choices.outcome: The shelter commits supplies to carrying meals to that door. The second place stays set.

choices.label: Persuade them to come to the shelter
choices.outcome: They are safe, and fed, and among people. The house is dark tonight for the first time.

missions.lead: The care note mentions medicine kept at the big house on the hill - the Halloran place.

missions.title: Enough for One More
missions.find: the neighbourhood medicine cupboard
missions.brief: The shelter is short of medicine and there is said to be a store of it in the Halloran Mansion. The house is not empty. Go carefully.
missions.discovery: Somebody kept a medicine cupboard for the whole neighbourhood after the clinics shut - labelled, dated, rationed. What is left in it is keeping one hidden patient alive.
missions.ask: The shelter needs all of it. The patient needs some of it.

choices.label: Take the stock for the shelter
choices.outcome: The shelter can treat people again. Nobody has been back to see how the patient is.

choices.label: Leave the patient's share
choices.outcome: You come back with less. One household that could not have asked is still there because of it.

missions.lead: A treatment note in the cupboard is signed by a shelter volunteer who never came back.

missions.title: The Room with the Light On
missions.find: the volunteer's notes, outside a closed bedroom door
missions.brief: One of our volunteers went out to a house call and stayed. Find them. Bring them home - if they will come.
missions.discovery: They are tending an empty bedroom, sure that someone in it needs them. Through the door you hear a voice say something only one person ever said to you. Nothing in the room proves who spoke.
missions.ask: They can be persuaded home, or helped to keep visiting.

choices.label: Persuade the volunteer to return
choices.outcome: The shelter has its best pair of hands back. The light in that bedroom is off.

choices.label: Support limited visits
choices.outcome: They go on believing, twice a week, at the cost of supplies the shelter could have used. They trust you completely.

missions.lead: The volunteer's notes mention letters - a drawer of them, at the shelter, that Kateryna never gave out.

missions.title: Letters Never Delivered
missions.find: a drawer of undelivered letters
missions.brief: There is correspondence in storage here that has not been given to the people it was written to. Before anything is done with it - check that one of them is still at the address.
missions.discovery: Kateryna kept back the letters that said someone had left, or died. She was afraid people would go, or give up. Some of what kept them safe was not being told about their own lives.
missions.ask: The letters can be delivered now, or left with Kateryna to give out in her own time.

choices.label: Deliver the letters
choices.outcome: People know. Some of them leave. The shelter has fewer hands and nobody in it is being managed.

choices.label: Leave delivery to Kateryna
choices.outcome: The shelter stays staffed. Kateryna decides, a letter at a time, who is ready to hear what.

missions.lead: One of the people those letters were for wants to leave the shelter, and has asked for help doing it.

missions.title: Leave the Light On
missions.find: a house that could be lived in again
missions.brief: That household wants to choose between staying here and going back to a house of their own. Look at the house. Whatever they decide, it is theirs to decide - help them do it.
missions.discovery: Staying is safer. They know that. What they want is a life that is not being looked after. Kateryna says nothing for a long time, and then says she is afraid that letting them go is the same as failing them.
missions.ask: This becomes how Residential looks after its own.

choices.label: Back independent living
choices.outcome: A house in Residential has a light in it again, and somebody in it who will trade with you. The shelter's reserves are lower.

choices.label: Help secure an agreed stay
choices.outcome: They stay, because they chose to. The shelter is stronger for it.

missions.title: Passage Owed
missions.find: the courier's payment ledger
missions.brief: A courier of mine is stranded out past the freight track with a payment ledger on him. Bring the ledger back and I will put you in touch with someone who knows the routes.
missions.discovery: Beside this year's debts are the first entries, from the night of the evacuation: paid with a watch; paid with two tins; paid - nothing. Some people were got out because they were neighbours.
missions.ask: The courier still owes the crew his own passage.

choices.label: Collect the courier's debt
choices.outcome: The crew is paid and thinks well of you. The courier works it off on the worst road they have.

choices.label: Waive it
choices.outcome: A smaller payout, and a guide in the Barrens who will always tell you which way is quiet.

missions.lead: The courier's cargo docket lists a delivery to the farm that was never paid for.

missions.title: Protection Money
missions.find: the farm's accounts
missions.brief: The farm has stopped paying in food. Go out with the collector and find out why. The routes there are contested - keep your head down.
missions.discovery: The guards the farm was paying for never came. The protection existed in the ledger and nowhere else.
missions.ask: The payment can be collected, or turned into the thing it was paying for.

choices.label: Enforce collection
choices.outcome: The crew eats better. The farm will not open its gate to you again without a reason.

choices.label: Redirect it into a real guard shift
choices.outcome: No commission. There are two rifles on the farm's fence tonight that were not there yesterday.

missions.lead: The guards who should have been at the farm went to meet someone coming out of the jail.

missions.title: A Door Left Open
missions.find: the guide's notes, and the map they drew
missions.brief: A guide of ours is accused of selling a route. They were last seen near the jail. Find them before the crew does.
missions.discovery: The guide gave away one path - to put a household back together that the cordon had split. The path is burned now. Saving one family has put everyone else who used it in the open.
missions.ask: The guide can be brought back to settle with the crew, or helped to go.

choices.label: Return the guide to settle the debt
choices.outcome: The crew keeps its routes and its discipline. The guide goes nowhere now without being told to.

choices.label: Help them leave
choices.outcome: You have a contact who owes nobody anything. The crew has closed its better routes to you.

missions.lead: The guide's notes say who bought the route. They were buying more than a route.

missions.title: The Price of a Name
missions.find: a ledger of travellers and where they were going
missions.brief: There is an exchange happening by the freight track - a ledger with travellers' names in it. I want it intercepted. Do not ask me why I know about it.
missions.discovery: Wade sold access to cover the crew's losses and told himself the buyer only wanted tolls. The buyer is using the families in it to lean on people. In a packed bag by the track a wind-up alarm clock goes off. Its owner is confirmed dead.
missions.ask: The ledger is worth a great deal to the buyer. Its pages are worth more to the people named on them.

choices.label: Sell the ledger
choices.outcome: A large payout and a seat with the buyer. Every name in it is somebody who can now be found.

choices.label: Return the pages to the people named
choices.outcome: People can travel without being followed home. There is no payment, and everyone now knows what Wade did.

missions.lead: The buyer has stopped asking. It is coming to the freight track to take its toll in person.

missions.title: Nobody Owns the Road
missions.find: the passage itself, and who is standing on it
missions.brief: A civilian shipment is going through the freight-track passage and the buyer says it is owed a toll. See the shipment through and settle the claim before the crews settle it their way.
missions.discovery: Wade can keep one road guarded and dependable by charging for it and letting nobody else use it - or break the monopoly, with too few people to promise anyone is safe on it.
missions.ask: This becomes how the Barrens are crossed.

choices.label: Uphold exclusive passage
choices.outcome: The road is guarded, and it costs what the crew says it costs.

choices.label: Open the road
choices.outcome: Anyone can cross for next to nothing. Some days there is an escort and some days there is not.

choices.label: Have the farm fund shared protection
choices.outcome: The farm feeds a small guard that answers to nobody's ledger. It costs the farm food every week, and they have agreed to it.
